This breaks encapsulation and should be avoided if possible, core code shouldn't include editor code

But if it is to be included it has to be guarded with `TOOLS_ENABLED`
Same here

```suggestion
			if (EditorSettings::get_singleton()) {
```
Or this will fail, copy past error I assume, also needs to be guarded like the include
Needs the same check as in dir access

Having it editor only is questionable in general. Instead, I would:
- move `get_global_resource_path` to `ProjectSettings` and add (unexposed to scripting) `set_global_resource_path`.
- editor init can use it to set editor specific path, and if it is not set, it will return the same path as `get_resource_path`.
Shouldn't it be `FileAccessUnix`?

ditto:

```suggestion
		Ref<DirAccess> global_dir = DirAccess::create(DirAccess::ACCESS_EDITOR_RESOURCES);
```

@@ -510,10 +527,15 @@ void EditorFileSystem::_scan_filesystem() {
 		Ref<DirAccess> d = DirAccess::create(DirAccess::ACCESS_RESOURCES);
body:
ditto:

```suggestion
		Ref<DirAccess> dir = DirAccess::create(DirAccess::ACCESS_RESOURCES);
```
This `#include` is only needed in the `.cpp` file right? IIRC such includes should be added in there, not in the header.

If the goal is to not include global addons in exported builds, they shouldn't be included when running the project either, right? Even if it's launched from the editor, the launched instance acts like a final game build, only in the context of being within a development environment.

Otherwise, I anticipate this may become a major source of confusion for users as to why exported builds might fail _(having `using UnityEditor;` Unity bugs flashbacks_ 🫣 _)_

Well, if the future goal is to prevent global resources to be added to project resources, [as mentioned here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/831#issuecomment-3703682084). Then this probably should not be a problem.

Probably. That might be why Linux build compilation failed.

Edit: I can confirmed that that is not why the linux compilation failed.
I think it should be called `scan_directory`.
This is not correct, you can't use `ERR_FAIL_NULL` with `Ref`
Ditto, should be `ERR_FAIL_COND(da.is_null())`

IIRC the Linux build performs some additional checks such as running unit tests with ASAN and checking class documentation. That's why those pipelines are failing; the Linux build compiles without issue.
Thanks, didn't know that

You need to update the class documentation (`doc/classes/ProjectSettings.xml`) with this change. See the [CI logs](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/20856560250/job/59924794816?pr=111193#step:22:38) for more details

This `editor_filesystem` needs to be deleted on the destructor as well (`EditorFileSystem::~EditorFileSystem()`). That's very likely the reason [ASAN is reporting a memory leak in the CI](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/20856560250/job/59924794778?pr=111193#step:20:288).

See my comment in the proposal.
Editor resources should not be available at runtime, so this needs to be removed.
This should also be eventually part of editor settings (I mean for `editor://`).

```suggestion
	const String editor_resource_path = EditorPaths::get_singleton()->get_data_dir().path_join("editor_resources").path_join(vformat("%d.%d", GODOT_VERSION_MAJOR, GODOT_VERSION_MINOR));
```
Does not need to be broken into 3 variables. Also `filename` is misleading here.

Also it should use the new constant from EditorPaths instead of hard-coding folder name.
The new condition makes the previous one redundant.
You can use `DirAccess::create_for_path()`.

The assign value only have have one `/`. So here is what I will use instead:

`path_write[0] = efd->root_path.trim_suffix("/");`
This code for the other paths (res:// and user://) are also the same as the current one, so I will also change those to your suggested change.
Assuming they're using `replace_first` that sounds good, it's not too noisy to do it outside the scope of this PR
I'm using `p_path.trim_prefix("editor://")` instead. It is way simpler.
No please use this code it's better, doing `trim_prefix` does more checking, in this case we know it's present so please use `substr`
Are you saying your code is better?
Yes, it does the same but doesn't do the checking to see if the prefix is present (similar code is used in other parts of your code, stripping `ref://` with `substr(6)`

-		<member name="debug/gdscript/warnings/directory_rules" type="Dictionary" setter="" getter="" default="{ "res://addons": 0 }">
+		<member name="debug/gdscript/warnings/directory_rules" type="Dictionary" setter="" getter="" default="{ "editor://": 0, "res://addons": 0 }">
 			The rules for including or excluding scripts when generating warnings, as a dictionary. Each rule is an entry consisting of a directory path (key) and a decision (value). When trying to generate a warning, the GDScript parser chooses the most specific rule, i.e. the most nested directory containing the script. If the decision is [b]Exclude[/b], warnings are not generated for this script. If the decision is [b]Include[/b] or the script doesn't satisfy any of the rules, the warning configuration specified in the Project Settings is applied.
 			It is recommended to include your own addons/libraries, either project-specific or actively being developed at the moment. Third-party or project-agnostic addons/libraries should be excluded, as they may be incompatible with the project's warning configuration.
 			[b]Note:[/b] It is not recommended to remove or change the rule for [code]"res://addons"[/code] as the project's warning configuration may break third-party addons. Instead, consider including individual addons, if necessary.

```suggestion
			[b]Note:[/b] It is not recommended to remove or change the rules for [code]"res://addons"[/code] and [code]"editor://"[/code] as the project's warning configuration may break third-party addons. Instead, consider including individual addons, if necessary.
```
